items.arabic: بِسْمِ اللَّهِ، تَوَكَّلْتُ عَلَى اللَّهِ، وَلَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ

transliteration.en: Bismillāh, tawakkaltu ʿalā Allāh, wa lā ḥawla wa lā quwwata illā billāh

translation.en: In the name of Allah, I place my trust in Allah, and there is no might nor power except with Allah.

text.en: Whoever says, when he leaves his house, “In the name of Allah, I place my trust in Allah, and there is no might nor power except with Allah,” it is said to him: you are guided, sufficed and protected.
text.ar: مَنْ قَالَ — يَعْنِي إِذَا خَرَجَ مِنْ بَيْتِهِ — بِسْمِ اللَّهِ تَوَكَّلْتُ عَلَى اللَّهِ وَلاَ حَوْلَ وَلاَ قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ

why.en: A sentence at the door that hands the day over to Allah before it starts. The Prophet ﷺ taught that whoever says it is guided, provided for and protected as they go out.

how.en: Pause at the door as you leave.
Say the words once, quietly or aloud.
Step out.

translation.en: O Allah, open for me the doors of Your mercy.

text.en: When one of you enters the masjid, let him say: O Allah, open for me the doors of Your mercy.

why.en: The masjid is a place of mercy, so you ask for mercy as you walk in. It also marks the change from the street to the prayer.

how.en: Step in with your right foot.
Say the dua as you enter.

items.arabic: سُبْحَانَ الَّذِي سَخَّرَ لَنَا هَذَا وَمَا كُنَّا لَهُ مُقْرِنِينَ وَإِنَّا إِلَى رَبِّنَا لَمُنْقَلِبُونَ

transliteration.en: Subḥāna-lladhī sakhkhara lanā hādhā wa mā kunnā lahu muqrinīn, wa innā ilā rabbinā la-munqalibūn

translation.en: Glory be to the One who has subjected this to us, when we could never have done it ourselves; and to our Lord we shall surely return.

text.en: When the Prophet mounted his camel to set out on a journey he would say: Glory be to the One who has subjected this to us, when we could never have done it ourselves.

why.en: The travel dua thanks Allah for the means of travel and asks for an easy road and a safe return. It is said once the journey is actually under way.

how.en: Once seated and moving, say Allahu Akbar three times.
Say the dua.
Ask for ease, safety and a good return in your own words if you like.

translation.en: In Your name, O Allah, I die and I live.

text.en: When the Prophet went to bed he would say: In Your name, O Allah, I die and I live.

why.en: The last words of the day, given to Allah. Saying them makes sleep itself an act of remembrance.

how.en: Lie down on your right side if you can.
Say the words once.

items.arabic: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي أَحْيَانَا بَعْدَ مَا أَمَاتَنَا وَإِلَيْهِ النُّشُورُ

transliteration.en: Al-ḥamdu lillāhi-lladhī aḥyānā baʿda mā amātanā wa ilayhi-n-nushūr

translation.en: Praise be to Allah who gave us life after causing us to die, and to Him is the resurrection.

text.en: When the Prophet woke he would say: Praise be to Allah who gave us life after causing us to die, and to Him is the resurrection.

why.en: Waking is a small return to life, and the first words of the day thank the One who gave it back.

how.en: Say the words as soon as you are awake, before anything else.

text.en: The Prophet said to a boy in his care: Say the name of Allah, eat with your right hand, and eat from what is nearest to you.

why.en: Naming Allah over food is the difference between eating and eating with gratitude. If you forget and remember mid-meal, there is a form for that too.

how.en: Say Bismillah before the first bite.
If you forget, say: Bismillahi awwalahu wa akhirahu (in the name of Allah at its beginning and its end).

text.en: Whoever glorifies Allah thirty-three times after each prayer, praises Him thirty-three times and magnifies Him thirty-three times, then completes the hundred, his sins are forgiven even if they are like the foam of the sea.

why.en: Thirty-three each of Subhan Allah, Alhamdulillah and Allahu Akbar after every prayer, completed with one phrase to make a hundred. The Prophet ﷺ said sins are forgiven for it, however many.

how.en: After the prayer, say Subhan Allah 33 times.
Say Alhamdulillah 33 times.
Say Allahu Akbar 33 times.
Complete the hundred with: La ilaha illa Allah wahdahu la sharika lah, lahu al-mulk wa lahu al-hamd wa huwa ala kulli shay'in qadir.

text.en: Allah — there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of existence.
Whoever recites Ayat al-Kursi after every obligatory prayer, nothing stands between him and entering Paradise but death.

why.en: One verse, recited after each prayer. The Prophet ﷺ said nothing stands between the one who recites it after prayer and entering Paradise except death.

how.en: After the tasbih, recite Ayat al-Kursi (Qur'an 2:255) once.

text.en: Were it not that it would burden my ummah, I would have ordered them to use the siwak at every prayer.

why.en: Cleaning the teeth before standing to pray. A toothbrush serves the same purpose where there is no siwak.

how.en: Before the prayer, clean the teeth with a siwak or a brush.

text.en: The two rak’ah before Fajr are better than the world and everything in it.

why.en: Two short rak'ah before the Fajr prayer. Of all the voluntary prayers, this is the one the Prophet ﷺ never left, even when travelling.

how.en: After the Fajr adhan and before the obligatory prayer, pray two rak'ah.
Keep them short.
Then pray Fajr.

text.en: Whoever prays twelve rak’ah in a day and a night, a house will be built for him in Paradise.

why.en: Two rak'ah after the Dhuhr prayer, part of the twelve daily rawatib for which the Prophet ﷺ promised a house in Paradise.

how.en: After the Dhuhr prayer and its dhikr, pray two rak'ah.

text.en: The best manner of seeking forgiveness is to say: O Allah, You are my Lord, there is no deity but You. You created me and I am Your servant.

why.en: A set of remembrances said between Fajr and sunrise, or in the morning generally. They frame the day before it fills with everything else.

how.en: After Fajr, sit a moment.
Say the morning adhkar: Ayat al-Kursi, the three Quls, the sayyid al-istighfar, and the rest.
If you know only one or two, say those.

text.en: The best manner of seeking forgiveness is to say: O Allah, You are my Lord, there is no deity but You. You created me and I am Your servant.

why.en: The evening counterpart, said between Asr and Maghrib or in the evening generally. The same protection and gratitude for the night as for the day.

how.en: After Asr, sit a moment.
Say the evening adhkar.
If you know only one or two, say those.

text.en: The Prophet was asked about fasting on Monday and said: that is the day I was born, and the day I was sent, or the day revelation came to me.

why.en: The Prophet ﷺ fasted Mondays and Thursdays and said deeds are presented on those days. Monday is also the day he was born.

how.en: Decide the night before to fast.
Eat before Fajr if you can.
Fast from Fajr to Maghrib.

text.en: Deeds are presented on Monday and Thursday, and I like my deeds to be presented while I am fasting.

why.en: Thursday is the other weekly fast the Prophet ﷺ kept. One day a week is a manageable habit; two is his own.

how.en: Decide the night before to fast.
Eat before Fajr if you can.
Fast from Fajr to Maghrib.

text.en: My friend advised me to do three things: to fast three days of every month, to pray two rak’ah of Duha, and to pray Witr before sleeping.

note.en: The hadith establishes fasting three days of each month. Scholars differ on whether these must be the thirteenth, fourteenth and fifteenth specifically.

why.en: Three days a month, on the 13th, 14th and 15th when the moon is full. The Prophet ﷺ compared fasting three days each month to fasting the whole year.

how.en: Watch for the middle of the Islamic month; this app shows it a few days ahead.
Fast the 13th, 14th and 15th, or any three days of the month.

text.en: The Prophet found the Jews fasting on the day of Ashura, and said: we have more right to Musa than you — so he fasted it and ordered that it be fasted.

why.en: The 10th of Muharram. The Prophet ﷺ said fasting it expiates the sins of the year before, and recommended adding the 9th.

how.en: Fast the 10th of Muharram.
Add the 9th if you can.

title.en: Fasting on the day of Arafah

text.en: Fasting the day of Arafah expiates the sins of the preceding year and the coming year.

note.en: Scholars differ on whether this follows the local ninth of Dhul Hijjah or the day of standing at Arafah in Makkah when the two fall differently.

why.en: The 9th of Dhul Hijjah, the day the pilgrims stand at Arafah. For those not on Hajj, fasting it expiates two years of sins.

how.en: Fast the 9th of Dhul Hijjah.
Not for pilgrims; they do not fast that day.

text.en: Whoever fasts Ramadan and follows it with six days of Shawwal, it is as though he fasted the whole year.

why.en: Six days of fasting in the month after Ramadan. With Ramadan they add up to what the Prophet ﷺ called fasting the whole year.

how.en: Any six days of Shawwal, together or apart, after the day of Eid.

text.en: My friend advised me to do three things: to fast three days of every month, to pray two rak’ah of Duha, and to pray Witr before sleeping.

why.en: A short voluntary prayer in the mid-morning. The Prophet ﷺ said the charity owed by every joint of the body is discharged by two rak'ah of Duha.

how.en: When the sun is well up and before midday, pray two rak'ah or more.

text.en: And when you travel throughout the land, there is no blame upon you for shortening the prayer.

note.en: Scholars differ on whether shortening on a journey is obligatory or a concession that may be taken or left.

why.en: On a journey the four-rak'ah prayers are shortened to two. It is a gift, not a compromise, and the Prophet ﷺ always took it.

how.en: While travelling, pray Dhuhr, Asr and Isha as two rak'ah each.
Fajr and Maghrib stay as they are.

text.en: I memorised ten rak'ah from the Prophet ﷺ: two before Dhuhr and two after it, two after Maghrib in his house, two after Isha in his house, and two before the Fajr prayer.

why.en: Two or four rak'ah before the Dhuhr prayer, the largest part of the daily rawatib. They settle you before the obligatory prayer rather than rushing into it.

how.en: After the Dhuhr adhan and before the obligatory prayer, pray two rak'ah, or four as two pairs.
Then pray Dhuhr.

text.en: I memorised ten rak'ah from the Prophet ﷺ: two before Dhuhr and two after it, two after Maghrib in his house, two after Isha in his house, and two before the Fajr prayer.

why.en: Two rak'ah after the Maghrib prayer. The Prophet ﷺ prayed them at home, which is where most people are at that hour anyway.

how.en: After the Maghrib prayer and its dhikr, pray two rak'ah.

text.en: I memorised ten rak'ah from the Prophet ﷺ: two before Dhuhr and two after it, two after Maghrib in his house, two after Isha in his house, and two before the Fajr prayer.

why.en: Two rak'ah after the Isha prayer, the last of the rawatib, usually prayed at home before Witr.

how.en: After the Isha prayer and its dhikr, pray two rak'ah.

text.en: Make Witr the last of your prayer at night.

why.en: An odd number of rak'ah, often one or three, as the last prayer of the night. The Prophet ﷺ never left it, at home or on a journey, and told us to make it the last thing we pray.

how.en: Any time after Isha and before Fajr, pray one rak'ah, or three.
If you fear you will not wake, pray it before sleeping.
Make it the last prayer of your night.

text.en: When a man enters his house and mentions Allah on entering and on eating, Shaytan says to his companions: you have no lodging here and no supper.

why.en: Mentioning Allah as you come in, and greeting whoever is there, keeps the home a place He is remembered in. The Prophet ﷺ said Shaytan finds no place to stay in such a house.

how.en: Say Bismillah as you step in.
Greet those inside with as-salamu alaykum, even if the house is empty.

text.en: When we went up we said Allahu Akbar, and when we came down we said Subhan Allah.

why.en: Allahu Akbar as you climb: a hill, a staircase, a lift. The companions did it on every rise of the road, and it turns an ordinary climb into remembrance.

how.en: As you start going up, say Allahu Akbar.

text.en: When we went up we said Allahu Akbar, and when we came down we said Subhan Allah.

why.en: Subhan Allah as you descend, the pair to the takbir on the way up.

how.en: As you start going down, say Subhan Allah.

items.arabic: بِسْمِ اللَّهِ، الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ، سُبْحَانَ الَّذِي سَخَّرَ لَنَا هَذَا وَمَا كُنَّا لَهُ مُقْرِنِينَ وَإِنَّا إِلَى رَبِّنَا لَمُنْقَلِبُونَ

transliteration.en: Bismillāh, al-ḥamdu lillāh, subḥāna-lladhī sakhkhara lanā hādhā wa mā kunnā lahu muqrinīn, wa innā ilā Rabbinā lamunqalibūn

translation.en: In the name of Allah, praise be to Allah. Glory to Him who has subjected this to us, and we could never have accomplished it by ourselves; and to our Lord we shall surely return.

text.en: Glory to Him who has subjected this to us, and we could never have accomplished it by ourselves; and to our Lord we shall surely return.
When the Prophet ﷺ mounted his camel to set out on a journey, he would say Allahu Akbar three times, then: Glory to Him who has subjected this to us...

why.en: The words the Prophet ﷺ said on mounting his camel, which fit a car, a bus or a train exactly as well: this was put at our service, and we could not have done it ourselves.

how.en: Once seated, say Bismillah.
Say Alhamdulillah.
Say the verse: Subhan alladhi sakhkhara lana hadha wa ma kunna lahu muqrinin, wa inna ila Rabbina lamunqalibun.

title.en: Before sleep: Ayat al-Kursi and the Quls

text.en: Every night when the Prophet ﷺ went to bed he cupped his hands, blew into them, recited Qul huwa Allahu ahad, Qul a'udhu bi Rabbi al-falaq and Qul a'udhu bi Rabbi an-nas, then wiped whatever he could of his body, beginning with his head and face and the front of his body, three times.
When you go to your bed, recite Ayat al-Kursi; a guardian from Allah will stay with you and no devil will approach you until morning.

why.en: A short set the Prophet ﷺ recited every night: Ayat al-Kursi, and the three short surahs beginning with Qul, blown into the hands and wiped over the body. He said a guardian stays with the one who recites Ayat al-Kursi until morning.

how.en: Recite Ayat al-Kursi (Qur'an 2:255).
Cup your hands, blow into them, and recite al-Ikhlas, al-Falaq and an-Nas.
Wipe your hands over as much of your body as you can reach, starting with the head and face.
Do the hands three times.

text.en: Whoever stands in prayer in Ramadan out of faith and seeking reward, his previous sins are forgiven.

why.en: The night prayer of Ramadan, prayed in congregation as Taraweeh or alone at home. The Prophet ﷺ promised forgiveness of past sins to whoever stands in it out of faith.

how.en: After Isha, pray Taraweeh at the masjid or some rak'ah at home.
Any amount counts; keep what you can keep every night.

title.en: The first ten days of Dhul Hijjah

text.en: There are no days in which righteous deeds are more beloved to Allah than these ten days.

why.en: The ten days leading to Eid al-Adha, which the Prophet ﷺ said hold deeds more beloved to Allah than on any other days. Fasting, dhikr and charity all count; the 9th is Arafah.

how.en: Say Allahu Akbar, la ilaha illa Allah, Allahu Akbar, wa lillahi al-hamd through the days.
Fast whichever of the first nine days you can.
Give something in charity.
